articleTitle: Research on Path Tracking Control Method of Fully Driven AUV under Ocean Current Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) play an important role in human understanding and management of the ocean. Fully actuated AUVs can achieve 6 degrees of freedom motion control, with high control accuracy and anti-interference ability, and have high application value in the field of underwater precision operations. This article vectorizes the modeling of a multi thruster fully driven underwater vehicle, establishes a path tracking error model in a non-projective Serret Frenet coordinate system, designs disturbance resistant kinematic and dynamic controllers using inverse control methods, and analyzes the stability of the designed controllers. The simulation results show that the controller can asymptotically stabilize path tracking error, velocity tracking error, and attitude tracking error.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of a Wheel-Fin Hybrid Amphibious Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The amphibious robot is capable of operating in terrestrial, aquatic and transitional areas, making it suitable for deployment in complex and unstructured and environment. To enhance the propulsion speed, obstacle surmounting ability and adaptability of amphibious robot, a wheel-fin hybrid amphibious robot is proposed in this paper. This design features a self-adaptive climbing wheel unit and a pair of bionic undulating fins, enabling the robot to achieve remarkable speed on both land and underwater, as well as excellent obstacle crossing and water-land transition capabilities. Additionally, the robot utilizes a unique tail wheel mechanism to adjust its heading angle. The structure design of the robot and separate propulsion units are introduced first. The multi-mode motion principle in various environments is analyzed, followed by the realization of the hardware mechatronic system. The performance of the robot in land propulsion, underwater propulsion, obstacle climbing, and cross-media movement was tested. The experimental results validated the design scheme and demonstrated that the robot possesses good maneuverability, high speed, and strong obstacle crossing ability, providing new insights for the development of practical high-performance amphibious robots.

articleTitle: Multi-AGV Coordination System Design Based on 3D SLAM, MQTT and WeChat Mini-program
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: As automation and intelligence levels increase, the application of multi-robot coordination systems in industrial and logistical fields is becoming increasingly widespread. This research is dedicated to the development of a centralized multi-AGV coordination system, comprising three interconnected subsystems. The configuration includes two AGVs: a master AGV equipped with a 3D LiDAR, and a slave AGV with a camera for vision-based tracking. The centralized control interface is designed which is based on the WeChat Mini-program implementing the MQTT protocol for control message transmission and the HTTP protocol for receiving AGV status information. The operational efficacy of the multi-AGV system is demonstrated through two distinct working processes, both of which have been rigorously tested to confirm the successful implementation of the system.

articleTitle: An Effective Autonomous Navigation Method Using 3D LiDAR for Orchard Picking Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Autonomous navigation is crucial for enabling orchard picking robots to operate independently, yet most existing approaches focus on centerline navigation, which does not cater to the specific requirements of picking tasks. To address the challenge, we propose an autonomous navigation method employing 3D LiDAR for orchard picking robots. The approach construct a global point cloud map of the orchard using the SLAM algorithm, followed by filtering ground points through the CSF algorithm. The remaining non-ground points are clustered using Euclidean clustering to compute multiple navigation target points. A point cloud alignment algorithm is then employed to determine the relative transformation between real-time scanned point clouds and the pre-constructed map, thereby providing precise localization information. Finally, path planning between multiple navigation points is executed within the Robot Operating System (ROS). Experimental validations in both simulation and real-world environments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving autonomous navigation for orchard picking robots.

articleTitle: A Two-stage Angiographic Parameter Calibration Method for Coronary Artery 3D Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Three-dimensional(3D) reconstruction technology of coronary artery allows doctors observe more intuitively thus compensating the limitations of X-ray coronary angiography. However, directly using the original parameters to reconstruct 3D vessels can lead to substantial errors due to factors such as surgical table movement, heart beating, and inaccuracies in clinical calibration. Therefore, calibration of imaging system parameters is crucial for accurate 3D coronary artery reconstruction. This paper proposes a novel method for reconstructing 3D coronary artery from two uncalibrated angiographic views. It thoroughly analyzes the projection principle of X-ray coronary angiography and performs coarse calibration using coronary tree topology constraints and epipolar constraints. Moreover, in addition to the traditional reprojection error, this method introduces vascular diameter error for fine calibration. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves more accurate reconstruction results in a shorter time, with a reprojection intersection over union (IoU) ratio of 0.872, thereby confirming the effectiveness of this approach.

articleTitle: Kalman Filter Adaptive Speed Tracking Control for High-speed Trains with Noise Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In this paper, high-speed train is regarded as a single prime point, a new tracking control method combining adaptive control and Kalman filtering is proposed. This paper solves the noise interference problem in the tracking control process of high-speed train. The method first linearises the original system, then uses Kalman filtering to do model estimation, and the controller is designed for the predictive model through adaptive control. Finally, MATLAB is used to simulate and verify the effectiveness of this method. This proposed method successfully solves the problems of nonlinearity, noise interference and unknown parameters in system. The error caused by resistance in the high-speed train tracking control process can be dealt with effectively.

articleTitle: Impedance Control for Human–robot Interactions Based on a Sliding-mode Disturbance Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper presents an impedance control approach for human-robot interaction (HRI) systems without using torque sensors. A sliding-mode disturbance observer based on super-twisting algorithm is proposed to estimate the input torque of human applied to the end-effector of robot. Based on a Lyapunov approach, sufficient conditions are obtained to make sure that the estimation errors can converge to 0 in finite time through selecting proper gains of the observer. The impedance controller is proposed by using the estimation results of human torque. Simulation studies are performed on a robotic system, which shows the effectiveness of both disturbance observer and impedance controller.

articleTitle: LiDAR-based Vehicle Localization and Velocity Measurement in Long Corridors
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper focuses on improving the roadside vehicle localization and speed measurement system for a security inspection company. First, a horizontally mounted LiDAR is added to the original system to meet the demand for whole-process vehicle detection in long corridors. A simulation environment is created using Webots, providing necessary data sources to test and validate algorithms, with ROS2(Robot Operating System 2) to enhancing real-time system performance and task prioritization management. Then, dynamic threshold is employed to identify the cab-trailer separation of truck and prevent the radiation exposure from X-ray machine to the driver during inspection. A weighted average fusion method, incorporating distance and intensity, is used to enhance the accuracy of the system’s detection scheme. Finally, experimental results show that the improved system has better accuracy, stability, real-time performance, and portability.

articleTitle: Research on Stochastic Dual Control Method of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Attitude Angle with Outliers
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper proposals a detection method for external noise, which can address the issue of the simultaneous existence of parameter uncertainty and outliers in the UAV attitude angle system. The distance and direction criteria can detect the outliers in system output, incorporates Kalman filtering to deal with the external noise and internal parameters of the system. Based on the method of detecting the outliers of the system, we propose a stochastic dual control method. The method's efficacy is validated via simulation.

articleTitle: SFDet: Similar Fusion 3D Object Detection Using 3D Point Cloud and Image
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The paper introduces a novel network designed to merge 2D camera visuals and 3D LiDAR data, aiming to enhance the detection of 3D objects. The proposed similarity fusion network offers a straightforward, low-complexity method for combining data from different vision sensors, enhancing the detection process. By fusing camera and LiDAR data before applying non-maximum suppression, and using a Cosine similarity-based approach for non-coupled vision feature fusion without the need for additional training, the network efficiently processes visual information. A specialized fusion detection head is also developed for accurate 3D object detection using the combined visual features. Extensive experiments on the KITTI object detection dataset demonstrate that this fusion technique substantially outperforms single-sensor detection methods, particularly in detecting smaller objects.

articleTitle: 3D Human Pose Estimation and Tracking based on Feedback Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: To address the challenges of 3D human pose reconstruction failures and multi-person pose tracking in natural scenes, the study introduces a feedback mechanism and pose tracking function based on mvpose model matching mechanism. In this study, we employ the extended Kalman filter to predict the current moment’s 3D pose hypothesis; this 3D pose hypothesis is aligned with the reconstructed 3D pose from the previous moment, ensuring temporal continuity and consistency. The 3D pose hypothesis is projected onto the camera view to enhance the model's performance in complex environments to achieve 2D pose fusion. In addition, it makes full use of the spatial information generated by the feedback mechanism and the re-id features matched across views to achieve 3D pose tracking and re-identification effectively. Experimental results show that the method effectively reduces the failure of 3D pose reconstruction caused by multi-person interaction scenarios and achieves 3D pose tracking and re-identification functions.

articleTitle: Optimizing the PID Control Algorithm of BP Neural Network Using Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In an effort to lower greenhouse gas emissions, domestic thermal power units are gradually developing huge capacities and high specifications. Increasing the efficiency of coal combustion places significant demands on thermal system control. High precision control is hard to obtain with the standard serial PID control method. The benefits of bp neural network are its quick learning rate and excellent capacity for autonomous learning. To create a better PID algorithm, combine the BP neural network with the algorithm. The starting weights of the PID neural network were derived from the ideal neural network through optimization using the particle swarm approach. In the dense-phase zone of a 300 MW circulating fluidized bed with left pant leg at various operating points, model system modeling of fuel and bed temperature is performed by MATLAB. The outcomes demonstrate how the PID neural network shortens response times and keeps the control quantity moving closer to the goal. Compared to traditional serial PID control, the control effect is faster, more reliable, and more accurate.

articleTitle: Two-stage Robust Optimal Power Flow for Distribution Network with Multiple Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: To improve the operating economy and decrease the unsafe operation problems caused by the uncertainty of photovoltaic (PV) output and load, this paper investigates the second-order cone programming (SOCP) technique and the two-stage robust optimization (TSRO) theory to study the optimal power flow (OPF) under multiple uncertainties. Firstly, this paper establishes the OPF model based on the SOCP and incorporates the OPF model into the two-stage robust optimization model. In the first stage, the objective function is to minimize the cost of energy storage charging and discharging, responding to the worst load forecasting and PV output. The output of PV and load demand is depicted by a novel uncertainty set. Taking the output power of the thermal power unit on operation day as the optimization goal, the recourse problem is proposed in the second stage. This TSRO model is solved by column and constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm. We validate the method in the improved IEEE-33 bus system. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of TSRO applied to optimal power flow.

articleTitle: An Identification Method of Origins for Rice Wine Based on Electronic Nose and Dot-Product Module
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Research on origin identification of rice wines provides an important perspective for food quality evaluation. The electronic nose (e-nose) has shown promising performance in food quality analysis when used in conjunction with data processing models. Therefore, a method that includes a self-developed e-nose system and a hybrid dot-product-residual network34 (DPResNet34) is proposed to effectively recognize the origins of rice wines. The results showed that, first, gas information on rice wines from different origins is acquired using the e-nose system. Second, effective features of the e-nose data are mined and modeled by the DP module. Finally, the best classification performance and good stability, with an accuracy of 97.46%, an F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-score of 97.52%, and a Kappa coefficient of 97.19%, are achieved by the e-nose and DPResNet34 model. In conclusion, effective identification of the origins for rice wines is achieved by the e-nose and DP-ResNet34, providing a theoretical analysis framework for quality assessment of rice wines.

articleTitle: Design, Fabrication, and Experiment of A Parallel Leg Module for Insect-scale Micro Bionic Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: To address the problems of complex structure, poor versatility, and cumbersome fabrication of existing micro-crawling robots, an insect-scale parallel leg module is proposed. The module is a general-purpose insect-scale micro-crawling module that can not only move independently but can also be used with multiple modules to create a wide range of robots that can be applied to accomplish different tasks. The insect-scale parallel leg module has a weight of 0.2 g and size of 1.5 ×0.8 ×2.5 cm and is driven by piezoelectric ceramics. The overall structure of the module consists of the piezoelectric actuator unit and the parallel leg unit, which are fabricated in an integrated manner using micromachining technology and lamination techniques. The prototype of the insect-scale parallel leg module and the experimental environment were built, the movement displacement of the piezoelectric actuator and the plantar of the parallel leg module were tested, and the independent motion capability of the prototype was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Research on Lightweight Fire Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of complex structure and heavy calculation of existing fire detection algorithms, a lightweight fire detection algorithm based on YOLOv5s is proposed in this paper. Considering the characteristics of rapid fire spread, the algorithm specifically optimizes the Backbone and Neck structure of YOLOv5s network to achieve rapid and accurate identification of initial flame and smoke. The basic idea of the algorithm is as follows: Firstly, the Conv module and C3 structure in C3darknet53, the backbone network of YOLOv5s, are replaced with GhostConv and C3Ghost respectively, and auxiliary feature maps are introduced to expand the receptor field of the backbone network and improve the detection efficiency; Secondly, Gsconv convolution is used to replace the conventional convolution operation, which can reduce the number of parameters and computation of the neck network while maintaining the semantic information connection of the channel. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm reduces the number of parameters by 44.4% and the amount of computation by 53.2%, while maintaining the stability of its performance, which makes the algorithm suitable for resource-constrained environment and can detect flame smoke quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Research on an Occlusion-Resistant Human Pose Estimation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The existing human pose estimation techniques are widely applied in sports, stage, and industrial settings. However, these scenarios often involve significant occlusion, leading to poor robustness. To solve this problem, this paper proposed a method for precise localization of keypoints on various parts of the human body using a framework based on Transformer and MLP-Mixer architecture for human pose estimation. A top-down method is utilized to enhance the prediction accuracy of human pose estimation; Transformer is utilized as the backbone for feature extraction to increase global receptive field; Spatial Attention is utilized to transform features into the token sequences representing different granularity of human substructures; Relationships between structures are learned by utilizing the MLP-Mixer structure to encode prior knowledge of human structure more effectively to combat occlusion. Finally, our human pose estimation model achieves a good balance between the 10.1G complexity and 75.1 AP under the public datasets and possesses occlusion resistance. We present some typical visualization results in occluded scenes, which are significantly superior to HRFormer. In the future, we aim to apply this technology to dance mapping.

articleTitle: Design of Wind Turbine Cabin Inspection Robot System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper designs a wind turbine cabin inspection robot system, which comprises three components: the robot body, the communication system, and the monitoring software. The robot body features an elliptical track and houses various sensors, including a visible light camera, an infrared camera, and a microphone. These sensors are used to capture real-time images, video, and sound data from inside the wind turbine cabin. The communication system enables the transmission of data and commands between the robot and the monitoring software. Inspection staff can remotely observe the internal conditions of the wind turbine cabin and control the robot's movements through the monitoring software, thus eliminating the need for on-site inspections. This intelligent and automated inspection method aligns with the future direction of industry development.

articleTitle: Reliable Multi-agent Task Coordination Management System for Logistics System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The global population is aging, leading to significant societal challenges, particularly in developed countries like Japan. This demographic shift exacerbates labor shortages, driving the demand for automation solutions such as warehouse logistics robots. Current robots often fail to consider real-world constraints, resulting in impractical applications. This paper introduces a dynamic path planning algorithm for multiple robots, accommodating continuous task additions while considering kinematic and spatiotemporal constraints. Despite using simple, small-scale robots and sensors, the system generates 2D maps and calculates optimal paths. The Car-like conflict-based search (CL-CBS) and Spatiotemporal Hybrid-State A* algorithms address collisions and kinematic constraints, optimizing paths with dynamic updates. Experiments demonstrate the system’s effectiveness in real environments, showing improved task allocation and robot efficiency.

articleTitle: An Attitude Control Scheme for Low Redundancy Micro-nano Satellites without Gyroscopes
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: XX-1 satellite is a micro-nano satellite with low control system redundancy, equipped with only one set of three-axis gyroscopes. How to achieve attitude control during satellite failures has become an important issue in control scheme. This article proposes an attitude control scheme for low redundancy micro-nano satellites under the condition of no gyroscope. When high-value components in the satellite attitude control system, such as gyroscopes, fail and there are no redundant components, the satellite only uses magnetometers to reconstruct the attitude determination system, which can achieve attitude determination under any attitude conditions. This paper divides the working modes of micro-nano satellites into different modes based on the control tasks. Corresponding control laws are adopted in different modes, and magnetic torquers and momentum wheels are used to generate corresponding control torques, thus forming a complete satellite attitude control scheme. This paper further proposes effective discrimination conditions and parameter design methods for various working modes. Mathematical simulation shows that the proposed scheme enables micro-nano satellites to recover from any attitude to a stable operating state without gyroscope, and has the ability to operate stably in orbit for a long time. The attitude control accuracy is better than 2°, and the attitude stability is better than 0.003°/s, greatly improving the satellite's ability to operate safely in orbit.

articleTitle: An Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Policy Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: An evolutionary algorithm with a policy network is proposed in this paper. Based on the numerous regeneration operators accumulated in the field of evolutionary algorithms, a method for adaptive selection of reproduction operations has been designed. By utilizing the performance of reproduction operations during the iterative process, the strategic network is trained to provide quantitative indicators for the efficient selection of these operations. The proposed algorithm has comparative advantages compared with various evolutionary algorithms in terms of performance on some widely used testing problems.

articleTitle: Rule Inference Network based on Improved Granular Ball Neighborhood Rough Set
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The rule inference network is benefiting from both the interpretability of RIMER and learning capability of neural network. However, the combinatorial explosion problem limits its application in some area. In order to alleviate this problem, this paper proposes a rule inference network based on improved granular ball neighborhood rough set. Firstly, granular balls with appropriate granularity are generated through further splitting utilized the accelerated method of searching for natural neighbors. Then the improved granular ball neighborhood rough set is utilized for attribute reduction to reduce redundant or irrelevant attributes, which reduces the number of rules in the belief rule base. Finally, the experimental results indicate that the proposed model can improve of the performance of attribute reduction, alleviate combinatorial explosion problem and improve the capability of the classification model.

articleTitle: Synchronization of coupled stochastic reaction-diffusion systems driven by G-Brownian motion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper deals with synchronization for a class of coupled stochastic reaction-diffusion systems driven by G-Brownian motion (G-CSRDSs, in short). The mean square exponential synchronization criteria for G-CSRDSs are firstly established by means of the weighted G-Lyapunov function method and inequality techniques. Finally, an example is given to verify the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Research on Cucumber Target Area Segmentation Algorithm Based on Flower-assisted Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Cucumber is one of the world's top ten vegetables, loved by people. Its planting area in China is extensive, especially in greenhouse planting. Nowadays, the introduction of agricultural picking robots in greenhouse cucumber planting has become a new trend, and the precise identification and localization of cucumber fruits is a prerequisite for the precise operation of picking robots. In this paper, for the problem that naturally grown cucumber fruits and stems and leaves are similar in color and obscure each other, which makes it difficult to accurately segment the cucumber target, based on the statistical data on the pixel ratio of cucumber flowers and fruits at the maturity stage of the sample image, a cucumber target area segmentation algorithm based on flower-assisted localization is proposed. Using the significant color features of cucumber flowers to complete the flower target detection, and mark the poles to determine the coordinates of the bottom of the cucumber; combining the pixel ratio of flowers and fruits, the cucumber target region image is cropped in the image and the target segmentation is carried out using the color threshold. The experimental results show that the color threshold segmentation accuracy of the cucumber target region segmentation algorithm based on flower-assisted localization reaches 84%, while analyzing the complexity of the algorithm, the efficiency of the algorithm is significantly improved compared with the traditional threshold segmentation algorithm.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control for Quadrotor UAVs with Variable Mass Load Based on Extended State Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The inherent underactuation and strong coupling characteristics of quadrotor UAVs make the design of their trajectory tracking controllers challenging. To address the issues of dynamic uncertainties and unknown external disturbances in quadrotor UAVs, this paper designs a trajectory tracking controller for quadrotor UAVs with variable mass loads based on the inner-outer loop control structure. An adaptive sliding mode controller based on an extended state observer is used in the outer loop to adaptively estimate the mass of the quadrotor UAV with loads and achieve trajectory tracking. In the inner loop, a composite fast nonsingular terminal sliding mode controller based on an extended state observer is employed to ensure stable tracking of the desired attitude angles. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed control scheme ensures high-precision trajectory tracking of the quadrotor UAV under variable load mass and disturbances, indicating the effectiveness and robustness of the controller.

articleTitle: SAT Problem Solving based on Hybrid Grey Wolf Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: A hybrid algorithm based on grey wolf optimization algorithm, genetic algorithm, and heuristic information is proposed for solving SAT problems. The algorithm is an incomplete algorithm. To solve the problem that the retention of dominant individuals in the standard genetic algorithm depends on selection probability, the grey wolf optimization algorithm is introduced into the crossover operator to increase the probability of inheriting dominant individuals to new generation. At the same time, there is also a significant randomness in mutation operation, which makes the entire algorithm prone to falling into local optima and the convergence speed is too slow. Therefore, in mutation operator, select those variables whose values can satisfy more clauses, to jump out of local optima while accelerating the convergence speed of the algorithm. Through comparative experiments, it was found that the algorithm proposed in this paper can quickly solve satisfying problems, and the algorithm is efficient and stable.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a Novel Hybrid Ankle Rehabilitation Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: To address the needs of stroke and ankle injury patients in ankle rehabilitation and training. This paper presents a hybrid P−3RP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>S ankle rehabilitation robot characterized by a simple structure and 3R1T degrees of freedom. The mechanism possesses a virtual motion center that can coincide with the center of the ankle joint. It can adapt not only to the size differences among individuals but also cover the range of ankle rehabilitation movements. Firstly, screw theory is applied to determine the degrees of freedom of the mechanism and the position of the rotation axis of the moving platform. Secondly, the inverse kinematics model of the mechanism is derived using the closed-loop vector method. Subsequently, the inverse kinematics simulation of the parallel mechanism is conducted using ADAMS simulation software. The simulation results are compared with the theoretical solution obtained from MATLAB to validate the accuracy of the inverse kinematics model. Finally, the workspace of the parallel mechanism is plotted in MATLAB using the boundary search method, and its range of motion is analyzed to meet the demands of ankle rehabilitation. The performance analysis of the mechanism is evaluated based on the local condition number of the velocity Jacobian matrix, showing that the motion performance is good.

articleTitle: Multiple Profile Analysis and Its Application in Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Sharing an account across multiple individuals ("profiles") is a common occurrence in many applications. This situation poses significant challenges for existing recommender systems, as the behaviors of different users are merged together. In this paper, we introduce the concept of profiles and propose a framework to automatically extract implicit profiles from an account's historical behaviors, using the spectral clustering algorithm combining multiple signals derived from the user behavior. This task is complex, requiring an analysis of behavior relevance, intricate user behavior patterns, and various rule constraints. Our experiments demonstrate that the framework significantly enhances existing recommendation algorithms. To our knowledge, this is the first formal attempt to address the implicit multi-profile problem. Our framework provides a foundation for further research to advance this area.

articleTitle: Soft Measurement Modeling of Production Line Equipment Based on ALGWO-Elman
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Due to the complexity and diversity of the devices and the limitations of the range and cost of sensor applications. Fault detection information cannot be obtained completely and accurately. To address the above problems, Grey wolf optimization algorithm for adaptive leadership Elman network (ALGWO-Elman) is proposed. The Elman network is first used as the infrastructure for the soft measurement technique. The Grey wolf optimization algorithm (GWO) is combined with Elman network to improve the learning ability and generalization of soft measurement techniques. Nonlinear convergence factor and changing the number of head wolves with iteration stages were introduced into the grey wolf algorithm to improve the convergence speed and prediction accuracy of the algorithm. Simulation analysis shows that the ALGWO-Elman prediction accuracy reaches 95.9%, which effectively improves the accuracy of equipment fault prediction compared to other intelligent algorithms.

articleTitle: Discrete-time Adaptive Dynamic Surface Control Method with Performance-prescribed for Dielectric Elastomer Actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a discrete control scheme based on performance-prescribed dynamic surface technology for adaptive neural network with implicit inverse compensation to address the control problem of dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs). Compared to continuous control, discrete control is more in line with the working rules of computers. Innovatively introducing performance-prescribed functions in discrete control systems, enabling tracking errors to converge within a preset range in advance, utilizing implicit inverse compensation for hysteresis nonlinearity, and integrating it into adaptive dynamic surface control methods to achieve precise control of DEAs. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme was verified based on the constructed dielectric elastomer driven motion experimental platform.

articleTitle: Multi-robots Path Planning and Mapping for Exploring Unknown Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This study focuses on improving multi-robots path planning and mapping efficiency for exploring unknow environment. By improving the conventional exploration algorithm based on frontier to adapt to multi-robot systems, the robots will explore different areas and dynamically fuse individual maps generated by each robot into a comprehensive global map. The study introduces a unique joint path planning mechanism for each robot, enabling dynamic optimization of exploration target points and minimizing redundant exploration. The improved approach significantly reduces exploration time and collision incidents, as demonstrated by experiments comparing single and multiple robot exploration scenarios.

articleTitle: Recovery Control of USV Based on DRL and LADRC under Environmental Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: A novel control approach merging deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) is proposed to improve the recovery success rate of underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) under environmental disturbances. Firstly, the USV’s three degree-of-freedom model and models of environmental disturbances are established. Aiming at recovery guidance for underactuated USVs, an improved line-of-sight (LOS) guidance law is adopted to calculate the desired heading angle and surge speed. Then, LADRC is used to stabilize the tracking errors of heading angle and surge speed, with the twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm adjusting its parameters in real time. Simulation results validate that the proposed approach is efficient in the recovery control of the USV and superior to conventional LADRC, even in the presence of complex environmental disturbances.

articleTitle: Research on Density Control of Coal Preparation Based on Fast Decoupling Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This article presents a split-range control strategy based on fast decoupling to address the issue of extensive online computation in multivariable predictive control for coal preparation's suspension density. By employing split-range control, the predictive model's operating variables are reduced by comparing the suspension density with the set value, thereby retaining the crucial operating variables that significantly influence the controlled variable. Less significant operating variables are treated as measurable disturbances for swift compensation, effectively decoupling the original multivariable control model into a combination of multiple single-variable control models. Consequently, a decentralized rolling optimization strategy is devised using these multiple single-variable control models. Simulation experiments have demonstrated the algorithm's ability to substantially reduce the computational burden of online optimization and shorten calculation time from 1.147s to 0.253s once, thereby meeting the rapid response requirements of industrial applications.

articleTitle: Assist-Arm Configuration Analysis for Dual-Arm Space Robots in Capture Task
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Space robots will play an important role in orbital missions in the future, and multi-arm space robots have a wider range of applications due to their flexible structure. For a dual-arm space robot performing capture task in the mission-arm and assist-arm mode, this paper firstly from an innovative perspective regards the combination of the assist arm and the actual base as a virtual base with adjustable dynamic parameters, and based on this, establishes the system dynamics model. Thereafter, the maximum contact force and the base attitude disturbance are derived as the indicators which are proved that different configurations of the assist arm can affect. Finally, through the simulation experiments, it can be seen that different configurations of the assist arm will have an impact on the capture task of the mission arm, especially for the base attitude disturbance caused by contact.

articleTitle: High-Precision 3-DOF Compliant Positioning Stage for Large Range Micro-Manipulation Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high-precision compliant mechanism-based 3-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) positioning stage with a large range and planar layout. The design incorporates a cartwheel revolute flexure and compound basic parallelogram (CBP) prismatic flexure modules arranged in series to establish a PPR-kinematic chain. Three such kinematic chains are symmetrically arranged at 120° to each other around the output platform. This design ensures large deformation and high dynamic performance while minimizing cross-coupling and parasitic motion. The compliance matrix method (CMM) is utilized to establish the stiffness model of the designed mechanism. Computational analysis is performed to validate the developed analytical model. Moreover, the reachable workspace, inverse kinematics, and dynamic performance of the proposed stage are investigated. A workspace of 4.6 mm × 5.1 mm × 83 mrad is achieved while maintaining a high natural frequency of 58 Hz. From the analysis, the proposed stage can be adopted in micro-manipulation applications that require high-precision motion over an extended range.

articleTitle: Real-time Point Cloud Registration for Vehicle Localization Based on Prior Map Dynamic Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: When utilizing large-scale point cloud data for localization, the density of the prior point cloud map often leads to prolonged loading times and extensive computational resource consumption, challenging the real-time requirements of vehicle localization. To address these issues, we propose a precise and robust LiDAR localization system based on dynamic map loading. We divide the prior map into voxel submaps based on point cloud segmentation. Through the processing of point cloud segmentation, some outliers and some noise points are filtered out, which will greatly improve the efficiency and accuracy of high point cloud matching. Then the local map is loaded in real time according to the position of the vehicle. The Normal Distribution Transformation (NDT) algorithm is used to register the LiDAR scan and the prior local map. Experimental results demonstrate that our enhanced algorithm significantly enhances real-time efficiency and positioning accuracy for vehicle localization in large-scale scenarios.

articleTitle: Learning to Avoid Collisions in Mobile Manipulator Reaching Task
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Planning a trajectory for a mobile manipulator to complete a task challenges extremely as the robot has high degrees of freedom (DoF), especially in an unstructured environment. In recent years deep reinforcement learning (RL) achieves excellent performance in control fields, this paper applies the state-of-the-art deep RL algorithms to solve whole-body motion planning and control problem for mobile manipulator reaching in different environments. The method generalizes the problem from collision-free environment to those with static or dynamic obstacles by using transfer learning. The experiments are evaluated in different environments and the results verify the feasibility.

articleTitle: Research on Motion Control of Autonomous Wheelchairs in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This study aims to develop an autonomously operated wheelchair. In comparison to the WHILL electric wheelchair, which is known for its excellent maneuverability and operability in the market, this study focuses on investigating the dynamic environment surrounding the electric wheelchair. It proposes a parallel movement control method, allowing the wheelchair to autonomously adjust its position relative to a companion, effectively achieving seamless switching between automatic and manual modes. Utilizing the WHILL electric wheelchair equipped with laser sensors for obstacle avoidance and companion tracking, real-world experiments were conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The development of this autonomously operated wheelchair significantly reduces the workload of caregiving personnel and ensures the safety of the elderly and disabled individual.

articleTitle: Top Layer Localization in Stacked PCB Boards Using YOLOv8 and Self- generated Data
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The traditional method of unordered grasping in machine vision requires the use of 3D camera scanning or vibration plates for template matching. Both of these require a high development cost. To achieve low cost, high efficiency in developing a visual positioning system for unordered grasping, this paper proposes a visual positioning system based on YOLOv8 and self-generated data. In this system, self-generated data is used to generate the data needed for YOLOv8 training, by taking single PCB materials in a fixed scene, and marking them, followed by the generation of simulated stacked materials images and corresponding label images with self-generated data. Finally, these images are imported into the YOLOv8 model for training, enabling the positioning of the top material. This method allows for the positioning of only the front and back of a single PCB material, the only time data is marked, and the deployment of the model. It significantly addresses the issues of data scarcity in industrial deep learning applications, such as long data collection periods, high data annotation costs, and data collection costs.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Vector Measurement Method for Accurate Laser Positioning System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The accurate laser positioning system (ALPS) is an emerging distributed large-scale laser positioning system, which has shown broad prospects in industrial production, navigation, and other fields. Addressing the issue of reduced measurement accuracy in complex large-space measurement scenarios due to laser signal obstruction encountered by traditional planar and spherical receiver units, this paper analyzes the measurement principle of ALPS. Based on omnidirectional photoelectric array units, a comprehensive vector measurement model is established, and a position and attitude calculation method for omnidirectional vector measurement is studied. Employing the Monte Carlo method based on statistical principles, the feasibility of the position and attitude calculation method is verified through simulation. Additionally, field experiments are conducted in conjunction with a laser tracking system to evaluate the absolute accuracy of the proposed model under point and attitude changes. The results indicate that the point accuracy exceeds 0.24mm with a standard deviation of less than 0.026mm. When attitude changes occur, the horizontal and pitch directions are superior to 0.28mm and 0.47mm, respectively, with standard deviations of less than 0.030mm and 0.032mm, meeting the system's sub-millimeter-level requirements and expanding the application scope of the ALPS system.

articleTitle: Rule Inference Network Model Based on Improved ReliefF
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The rule inference network model, which integrates the RIMER and BP neural network, enhances the interpretability of neural networks. However, the problem of exploding rule combinations emerges, leading to dimensionality catastrophe. Aiming to the problem, this paper introduces a rule inference network model based on improved ReliefF. Firstly, it proposes the ReliefF algorithm utilizing clustering-based sampling and adjusted cosine similarity for attribute reduction, thereby alleviating the problem of rule combination explosion. Secondly, it establishes a belief rule base based on improved ReliefF. Then, the parameters are training for the belief rule base generation, which has fewer parameters due to attribute reduction. Finally, comparison experiments demonstrate that the rule inference network model based on improved ReliefF effectively alleviates the problem of rule combination explosion, enhancing training efficiency and improving classification performance of the model.

articleTitle: An Improved Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm for Multi-robot Path Planning under Complex Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In this work, we study path planning for multi-robot systems under complex tasks, which are given by global high-level specifications represented as Boolean formulas. This paper proposes a path planning method based on an improved ant colony optimization algorithm to compute the trajectory of each robot, ensuring that the total trajectories of the team fulfill the Boolean specifications while minimizing the total motion cost. The algorithm introduces a neighborhood search mechanism to enhance the neighborhood search capability. In addition, it incorporates an elite strategy to improve the qualities of the offspring populations and algorithm convergence speed. Simulation results show that compared with the Boolean specification-based multi-robot system path planning method using simulated annealing, the improved algorithm reduces the convergence time and minimizes the cost of the team. The solution time is shorter and the solution quality is higher, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in solving the path planning problem for complex multi-robot tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Rolling Generation Technology of Disaster Scene Panoramic Map based on Multiple Drones
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The limited monitoring range and lack of global electronic maps greatly restrict the effectiveness of large-scale and regional malignant disaster response by a single drone. Aimed to these issues, this paper proposes a rapid panoramic map generation technology based on multiple drones. The images of multiple drones are fused and spliced to form a panoramic map which is updated rollingly. Based on these, the passable areas are identified and labeled. This technology greatly improves the efficiency and safety of firefighters in carrying out reconnaissance and monitoring tasks, and lays the foundation for subsequent path-planning for relevant personnel or equipment.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-based Frequency Control for Renewable Energy Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: With extensive access to renewables, the inertia of microgrid is significantly reduced, which in turn puts forward higher requirements for the frequency stability of the system. In this paper, a frequency control method based on reinforcement learning is proposed for the intermittent and unstable characteristics of renewables. First, the microgrid frequency control principle and reinforcement learning theory are introduced. On this basis, a microgrid frequency control strategy based on Q-learning algorithm is proposed, and the design process is described in detail, including the design of the action set, state set, and reward function. Finally, the Q-learning algorithm is pretrained offline through simulation experiments, and tested in several scenarios for online operation. The effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed algorithm are verified through comparative analysis with other strategies.

articleTitle: Design of a Position Tracking Controller for Quadrotor UAVs with Variable Mass
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This study addresses the trajectory tracking challenges of quadcopter unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in the presence of load mass variations and disturbances. It introduces a position controller design based on integral backstepping and adaptive control. By incorporating horizontal and vertical position controllers along with a mass observer, precise trajectory tracking control of the UAV is achieved. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to existing control methods, the proposed controllers can rapidly and accurately estimate the UAV's mass variations under both gradual and sudden changes, effectively reducing tracking errors and enhancing control performance. This research offers an effective control strategy for addressing the trajectory tracking issues of quadcopter UAVs during load-variable missions.

articleTitle: A Predictive Control Method for Human-following Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Human-following mobile robot is widely applied in our daily life and work. The precision and security of the human-following behavior is decreased by the slow response of commonly-used passive control method. A novel predicative control method is proposed in this paper. In this method, the robot use a inverted pendulum model to predict human motion at first. Based on the prediction, model predictive control (MPC) helps to plan the motion of robot by summarising the human-following behavior of mobile robot as an optimization issue. Experiments are performed to make a comparison between the effectiveness of the proposed control method and that of virtual spring method, a commonly-used human-following control method. During these experiments, the mobile robot followed human to pass through paths in different shapes. The results show that the precision and security of human-following behavior of the mobile robot is increased with the help of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Hierarchically Decentralized Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Task Allocation System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: With plans to send humans to the Moon and further, the supply of resources like oxygen, water, fuel, etc., can be satiated by performing In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), where resources from the extra-terrestrial body are extracted to be utilized. These ISRU missions can be carried out by a Multi-Robot System (MRS). In this research, a high-level auction-based Multi-Robot Task Allocation (MRTA) system is developed for coordinating tasks amongst multiple robots with distinct capabilities. A hierarchical decentralized coordination architecture is implemented in this research to allocate the tasks amongst the robots for achieving intentional cooperation in the Multi-Robot System (MRS). 3 different policies are formulated that govern how robots should act in the multiple auction situations of the auction-based task allocation system proposed in this research, and their performance is evaluated in a 2D simulation called pyrobosim using ROS2. The decentralized coordination architecture and the auction-based MRTA make the MRS highly scalable, reliable, flexible, and robust.

articleTitle: Heuristic Sampling for Robot Motion Planning via Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks in Narrow Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Sampling-based motion planning methods are widely used in the robotics community but often exhibit diminished performance in narrow spaces. Despite efforts to enhance planning efficiency by introducing various sampling strategies aimed at increasing the likelihood of sampling within narrow spaces, these approaches are often tailored to specific planning problems, limiting their generalizability. Here, we present a motion planning algorithm employing heuristic sampling via Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN), which leverages insights from previous successful plans to predict potential regions containing feasible paths for new planning problems. By utilizing such prior information to guide sampling, our approach enables motion planners to rapidly identify feasible paths, even in complex environments. Through extensive simulation experiments, we demonstrate the computational efficiency of this sampling strategy.

articleTitle: Elastic Pyramid Elements for Constructing Spherical Parallel Continuum Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to designing Parallel Continuum Robots (PCRs) with spherical movement. Pyramid elastic units are used to construct limbs with special kinematic characteristics for the PCR. By developing and characterizing various elastic units with unique mechanical properties based on finite element analysis (FEA), we can identify effective designs for targeted robot motion. The kinetostatics model of the limbs is built based on the compliance analysis of the units, enabling the forward and inverse kinetostatics modeling of the whole robot. A series of 3-rotational PCRs are established using the designed elastic units, and mathematical experiments and simulations are conducted based on the selected units and PCRs. The computational results demonstrate good accordance with numerical analysis outcomes.

articleTitle: Observer-based global adaptive consensus tracking control for nonlinear multi-agent systems
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This article delves into the global leader-following consensus issue for second-order nonlinear multi-agent systems(NMASs), which are characterized by the presence of unknown nonlinear functions, unmeasured states, unknown disturbances and unknown control directions. To address these nonideal factors, a method integrating fuzzy logic systems and observers are deployed to manage the uncertainties arising from nonlinear functions and unmeasurable states. A signal substitution approach is adopted, utilizing the leader's information to determine the approximation domain, while Nussbaum gain functions are incorporated to address the unknown control direction. Ultimately, a fuzzy adaptive control protocol is tailored for each follower agent, ensuring that all signals in the closed-loop system achieve global uniform ultimate boundedness(GUUB), with the consensus error converging to a small neighborhood of the origin. Finally, the effectiveness of this approach is validated through simulation examples.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Objective Optimization Method for Ship Tank Loading Based on Improved Non-dominated Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Ship tank loading and unloading is one of the most frequent and typical operational scenarios. Meanwhile, ship loading and unloading operations are influenced by various factors such as meteorological and hydrological conditions in the operational waters, operational safety redundancy, operational windows, and more, all of which place extremely high demands on the efficiency and reliability of the loading plan. To improve the efficiency of ship tank loading and enhance control over the safety of the loading process, this paper constructs a complex loading condition characterized by calibrated loading capacity and floating state. An optimization model for ship tank loading plans is proposed, aiming to optimize the strength of the loading state. Based on the characteristics of this model, multiple optimization objectives and boundary conditions are sorted out. The NSGA-III method adapted to the specific needs, is used to facilitate the iteration of effective populations, thereby enabling the rapid generation of loading plans. This approach changes the traditional process of generating loading plans through multiple interactive iterations of first loading and then verifying against loading targets. Instead, it first determines the loading targets and then uses algorithms to find the optimal loading plan, improving the purposefulness of the loading work and optimizing the search process for loading plans.

articleTitle: Aerodrome Traffic Pattern Trajectory Prediction Based on Koopman Neural Operator
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Accurately predicting aerodrome traffic pattern trajectories is a crucial and challenging task in aviation operation optimization. To address the problem that the currently commonly used flight trajectory prediction methods cannot maintain high accuracy in aerodrome traffic pattern trajectory prediction, an aerodrome traffic pattern prediction method based on Koopman neural operator is proposed. Firstly, the low-dimensional nonlinear aerodrome traffic pattern is stacked into the Hankel matrix, and the potential dynamical system is found by SINDy; Second, a linear Koopman neural operator of size o × o is trained to move this system forward to realize the prediction; Finally, the prediction results are obtained by reflecting the dynamical system to the original space. The experimental results show that the KNO model performs better in the evaluation indexes of MAE, RMSE, and MAPE in the take-off, turn, and landing phases with maneuvering control compared with the excellent trajectory prediction models of the moment, CNN_LSTM, Informer, and TCN models, which can effectively realize the flight trajectory prediction and guarantee the safety of flight.

articleTitle: Substation Inspection Robot Location Method Based on Improved Particle Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The appearance of substation inspection robot marks the great leap of intelligent automation in the field of substation maintenance. Compared with the traditional manual inspection method, it has the advantages of high efficiency, low cost and improved personnel safety. In order to further improve the positioning accuracy of the robot, this paper first adjusts the relevant parameters in real time on the basis of the elementary particle swarm optimization algorithm to obtain more accurate estimation results. Secondly, aiming at the problem of low location of the basic particle filter algorithm and combining the advantages of particle swarm optimization algorithm, a new improved particle filter algorithm is proposed. Finally, the improved algorithm is applied to the location of substation inspection robot, and compared with extended Kalman filter, unscented Kalman filter and elementary particle filter, the effectiveness of the improved algorithm is verified.

articleTitle: Inverter Open Circuit Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Residual Performance Evaluation via Hypothesis Test
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In the analytical model-based fault diagnosis system, in order to manifest the fault information contained in the residual signal and realize the fault diagnosis under the condition of given fault detection rate, a residual evaluation fault diagnosis method based on hypothesis test was proposed for the open circuit fault diagnosis of NPC three-level inverter. Firstly, the parity space method was used to equalize the inverter system, obtain the state variable estimate to achieve analytic reconstruction, and calculate the residual through the parity vector. Next, the residual signals were divided into samples. The statistical characteristic of each sample was calculated as the residual performance. The threshold was calculated according to the probability distribution obeyed by the samples and the given fault alarm rate. The fault detection was realized by comparing the threshold and residual performance. The simulation and experimental platform results show that the proposed method can achieve fault detection under the specified fault diagnosis rate. The maximum diagnosis time is not more than three fourths of the fundamental wave period.

articleTitle: Time-Jerk Optimal Trajectory Planning of Robot based on Dung Beetle Optimizer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: To address the issues of low efficiency and vibration caused by motion impact in robotic operation, a time-jerk optimal trajectory planning method based on the dung beetle optimizer (DBO) algorithm is proposed. Initially, the trajectory of joint space motion is constructed using the 3-5-3 polynomial interpolation method. Then, the time and jerk of robot motion are taken as optimization objectives, with the joint velocity of the robot as a constraint in the optimization problem. The DBO algorithm, initialized with the logistic-tent chaotic mapping, is utilized to optimize these objectives. Simulation and experiments on the UR5 robot demonstrate that the overall motion time of the robot and the maximum jerk on each joint during motion are significantly reduced after optimization using the DBO algorithm, effectively enhancing the operational efficiency and motion stability of the robot.

articleTitle: Fast-PCANet For Scene Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: An efficient scene change detection algorithm based on Fast-PCANet is proposed. Given infrared and visible differential images, image blocks with candidate changed points can be distinguishes roughly from the unchanged pixel points by the calculated pixel classification threshold. As for Fast-PCANet which preserves detailed information and improves detection efficiency, feature maps of two principal component analysis convolutional layers are merged and concatenated to one dimensional feature vector, then a linear support vector machine is used to predict those changed pixels. The morphological closed operation and median filter are used to further correct false positives. For training Fast-PCANet, the proportion of negative samples is increased by sampling pseudo-changed points with a second-order arithmetic sequence, which can achieve the balance of between positive and negative samples. Experimental results shows the proposed algorithm effectively eliminates missed and false detection and and improves detection performance.

articleTitle: An Efficient Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Analytical Inverse Kinematics of Redundant Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In this paper, a Cauchy refraction-based Artificial Bee Colony algorithm (CRABC) is proposed for analytical inverse kinematics of redundant manipulators. Based on ABC, refracted opposition-based learning strategy and Cauchy operator are combined to design a food source update strategy, which can enhance the convergence accuracy and speed. In addition, in the scout bee phase, a new individual is generated by the proposed update strategy rather than random generation. To verify the effectiveness of CRABC, a 6-DOF manipulator was used to explore its inverse kinematics problem whose solutions need to meet the requirements of accuracy, continuity and real-time performance. A fitness function consisting of position accuracy and joint variation is proposed for solving the designed minimization optimization problem, where joint variations are set as a penalty term for the constraint processing. We compared CRABC with classical ABC and other intelligent optimization algorithms on a single target point, a straight trajectory and a circular trajectory. The results show that CRABC has high position accuracy and smooth joint movement in solving the inverse kinematics problem, and is very suitable for the operation tasks that require high accuracy.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Reinforcement Learning Techniques in Simulated Robotics Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Machine learning is a critical component of artificial intelligence and computer science that uses data and algorithms to emulate the way that humans learn and predict. Reinforcement learning, one of the many forms of machine learning, trains an agent through trial and error, with successful outcomes being rewarded and unsuccessful outcomes being penalized. The implementation of three reinforcement learning algorithms, Qlearning, Deep Q-Learning, and Double Deep Q-Learning, was tested using a series of ROS (Robot Operating System) packages in the Gazebo simulation environment. The Python openai_ros package and Gym libraries were used to input a robot into a configurable environment and test out the performance of a specific reinforcement learning algorithm. The agent’s action space was discretized into three specific actions, move forward, turn left, or turn right, that the robot could take. The reward or punishment was given after each step based on if the current action moved the robot towards the goal state or away from it. For each algorithm, the agent was first pre-trained on an obstacle free environment for 200 episodes and then was placed in an environment with two box-shaped obstacles to avoid. The algorithm/neural network parameters from the pre-training environment were loaded prior to the agent being tested in the new environment. The goal state at each episode was randomly generated and the robot’s performance was evaluated using the cumulative reward achieved per episode and the number of times it reached the goal.

articleTitle: A Review of Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control for Road Vehicles with Network Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Cooperative adaptive cruise control (CACC) allows connected vehicles in a platoon to maintain smaller headway, which has the potential to enhance driving safety and traffic efficiency. However, various network uncertainty in internet of vehicles, such as communication delay, network attacks, packet loss, can seriously affect the performance of CACC. In this paper, we focus on the research progress of CACC for road vehicles with network uncertainty. Basic issues including information flow topology, inter-vehicle spacing policy, and string stability of platoon are systematically discussed. This paper comprehensively reviews three important aspects of CACC for road vehicles with network uncertainty: communication delay, network attacks and packet loss. Finally, the future research direction of CACC is summarized and prospected.

articleTitle: DDPG-based Reactive Power Optimization Strategy For Active Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: To tackle challenges such as voltage fluctuations and network losses arising from integrating distributed energy resources into the grid, this paper proposes a novel reactive power optimization approach for active distribution network based on deep reinforcement learning. Diverging from conventional methods, our approach models reactive power optimization as a constrained Markov decision process, encompassing the determination of reactive power outputs from photovoltaic sources and compensation devices. By employing a deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm, the agent learns to make daily decisions based on the state of the environment. The methodology incorporates distributed control by training the agent to formulate optimal coordination strategies for photovoltaic inverters and capacitors. The efficacy of our proposed method is demonstrated by a comprehensive analysis conducted on a modified IEEE 33-node distribution network. The results highlight the superior performance in reducing active losses and mitigating voltage offsets compared to conventional methods.
